title: Organ Systems in Animals
seo_title: Biology 2: Organ Systems in Animals Worksheets (Strengthened SHS)
standard_text: Organ systems in animals: digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems, and how their structure fits their function; health and disease. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Biology 2, Quarter 4)
meta_desc: Free Biology 2 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 4): digestion and enzymes, the respiratory system, gas exchange, the heart and blood vessels and blood and health. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Digestion, respiration and circulation work together to supply every cell.
key_sub: Large surface areas and short distances make exchange fast.
body_html:
How to think about it

The digestive system breaks large food molecules into small ones (amylase: starch to sugars; protease: proteins to amino acids; lipase: fats to fatty acids and glycerol) that are absorbed through the villi of the small intestine.

In the lungs, oxygen diffuses from the alveoli into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out. The heart pumps blood in two circuits: the right side sends it to the lungs, the left side to the body. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins bring it back, and capillaries are where exchange happens.

Example

Which enzyme starts digesting starch in the mouth?

Starch is a carbohydrate.

Answer: salivary amylase

Example

Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than the right?

The left side pumps to the whole body.

Answer: it must pump blood at higher pressure around the body

Common mistakes

  • Saying arteries always carry oxygen-rich blood: the pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood.
  • Thinking digestion happens mainly in the stomach: most absorption is in the small intestine.
  • Mixing up breathing (moving air) and respiration (releasing energy).

faq.a: A short diffusion distance lets oxygen and carbon dioxide move between air and blood quickly.
They give the small intestine a huge surface area for absorbing digested food.

items.q: Cardiac output is 11.0 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 110 cm³. Calculate the heart rate.
